title: Learned artifact localization supports a bounded radiotherapy-dose comparison
summary: An Inception-V3 classifier localized dental artifacts in CT images. In fifteen separate head-and-neck treatment plans, its outputs guided comparisons of artifact-management choices; calculated target-coverage differences stayed below 0.25 percentage points. This is a retrospective planning result, not measured delivered-dose equivalence or evidence of safer treatment.
organization: University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

evidence.tested: Classifier development used 549 patients with patient-separated partitions. Fifteen other plans supplied comparisons of calculated dose after model-guided artifact localization.
evidence.unknown: One institution and planning system; no independent physical dosimetry, clinical outcomes or general treatment recommendation. Dose calculations are comparisons between modeled management scenarios.
evidence.ai_role: The learned slice classifier identifies locations used to define the compared artifact-management regions.

source_review.scope: Indexed primary full clinical/model Methods and dosimetric Results/discussion; exact front identity/date and current primary notice metadata.
